module_title: Memory Units - Higher Capacities and Exponential Conversions
introduction: This intermediate tier targets the massive storage units beyond Gigabytes. It also breaks down the exponential (Power of 2) conversion formats, which are frequently used by examiners to increase the difficulty level of standard conversion questions.

core_concepts.title: Higher Memory Hierarchy (TB to YB)
core_concepts.description:
The sequence continues beyond GB:
- 1 Terabyte (TB) = 1024 GB
- 1 Petabyte (PB) = 1024 TB
- 1 Exabyte (EB) = 1024 PB
- 1 Zettabyte (ZB) = 1024 EB
- 1 Yottabyte (YB) = 1024 ZB (Generally considered the largest officially accepted standard unit).

core_concepts.title: Conversions in Powers of 2
core_concepts.description:
Examiners often replace '1024' with its binary power equivalent:
- 1 KB = 2^10 Bytes
- 1 MB = 2^20 Bytes
- 1 GB = 2^30 Bytes
- 1 TB = 2^40 Bytes

core_concepts.title: Decimal Approximations (Powers of 10)
core_concepts.description:
Sometimes questions ask for rough decimal equivalents:
- 1 KB is approximately 10^3 Bytes (One Thousand Bytes).
- 1 MB is approximately 10^6 Bytes (One Million Bytes).
- 1 GB is approximately 10^9 Bytes (One Billion Bytes).

important_entities.name: The Million/Billion Rule
important_entities.key_fact: Standardized Terminology for MB and GB
important_entities.significance: In statement-based questions, 1 MB is universally referred to as 'One Million Bytes'. Similarly, 1 GB is referred to as 'One Billion Bytes', and 1 TB is 'One Trillion Bytes'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will deliberately skip a unit step to confuse you. Example: 'How many Bytes are in 1 MB?' If you rush and say 1024, you are wrong. 1 MB = 1024 KB, and each KB has 1024 Bytes. Therefore, 1 MB = 1024 x 1024 Bytes (or 1,048,576 Bytes).
Candidates frequently swap Petabyte (PB) and Exabyte (EB) in ordering questions. Remember the strict sequence: T (Tera) -> P (Peta) -> E (Exa).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Kings Make Great Toys, Pets Expect Zany Yoyos
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: K (KB) -> M (MB) -> G (GB) -> T (TB) -> P (PB) -> E (EB) -> Z (ZB) -> Y (YB).

exam_strategy_tips: If a question asks '2^30 Bytes is equal to what?', use your fingers to count up by tens: 10 (KB) -> 20 (MB) -> 30 (GB). Thus, the answer is 1 GB.
